transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Cole, Ravi Patel, Tara Nguyen (Redwood) — Maria Lopez, Ethan Chu, Sophie Grant, Liam Walker (Pinegrove)

Summary (auto): kickoff to align on onboarding, network/connectivity and pilot plan. Discussed hosted vs dedicated, VPC options, security artifacts, pilot success criteria, and next steps.

[00:00] Jenna: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm jenna cole from Redwood Inference, i'll kick us off. we planned about an hour, want to make sure we cover deck, then network requirements and pilot scope. ravi and tara from our side too.
[00:22] Maria: hi thanks, excited — quick context, Pinegrove is building a customer support summarization pipeline and a risk-detection assistant. we need low latency for chat in prod, and strict data residency for financial PII.
[00:37] Ravi: great, thanks. can you say a little bit about traffic volumes and qps expectations? that drives host vs dedicated sizing.
[00:45] Maria: for the first phase, about 200 qps at peak, but more like 40 sustained, we expect spikes during market opens; if we go wider in phase two, that could be 800+ burst.
[01:05] Ethan: also want to note we run in AWS us-east-1 predominantly, some eu-west-1 for EMEA, and we have a VPC with strict egress rules.
[01:18] Tara: perfect, that's helpful. architecture choices: hosted API will get you started fastest; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and you can reserve GPU pools. for banking-y workloads, most customers trend toward Dedicated or Private with VPC peering.
[01:40] Sophie: security is the big one. do you support KMS/HSM integrations for key management and can logs be forwarded to our SIEM?
[01:48] Jenna: yes on both — our Private offering supports customer-managed KMS and HSM attachments in the private control plane; for hosted we encrypt at rest and we provide audit log exports to S3 or SIEM connectors. we'll send the SOC2 package.
[02:05] Liam: sounds good. also curious about token-level cost and latency visibility, for our finance people.
[02:12] Ravi: console shows token breakdown per route and per-model latency percentiles; we'll share a sample dashboard screenshot.
[02:22] Jenna: quick note on fallback policies — we can set routing to cheaper quantized variants if Dedicated capacity is saturated, with automatic fallback. sometimes names get fuzzy in transcription — our product is Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private, not redwood-infer, just to call out.
[02:45] Maria: haha noted — we saw a benchmark where latencies for your hosted api averaged 60ms per token, is that right?
[02:54] Ravi: that depends on model and sequence length; for shorter chat turns, optimized kernels and continuous batching can hit low single-digit token latencies; the benchmark you saw may have been for larger context windows. we'll calibrate with your prompts.
[03:15] Ethan: on the networking side, we need explicit egress IPs for allowlist and TLS inspection. can you provide static egress ranges for Dedicated or for Private peering?
[03:28] Ravi: for Private we do VPC peering so traffic stays in your VPC, egress is on your side; for Dedicated we publish egress ranges for managed endpoints. i'll attach the network checklist after the call.
[03:45] Sophie: audit logs — retention windows, are they configurable? we need 7 years for certain logs for one of our regs.
[03:54] Tara: retention for audit logs in hosted is configurable up to a year by default; for enterprise packages in Private we can provide longer retention and archiving to customer S3 for unlimited retention. we'll include options in the whitepaper.
[04:13] Maria: good. now on pilot scope, we want to run a 2-week pilot that exercises 3 routes: chat summarization, risk classifier rerank, and embeddings for search. success criteria are: p95 latency under 400ms for chat, classifier AUC improvement > 5% over baseline, and embedding recall within 2% of current vector store.
[04:42] Jenna: that sounds concrete, love it. typical pilot we do: 2 week reserved Dedicated capacity or a Private trial, run benchmarks and joint evals, then a readout. do you have stakeholders and timeline?
[04:55] Maria: leadership wants a go/no-go in 6 weeks. that gives us time for pilot plus a security review.
[05:05] Liam: also procurement will need a data processing addendum and an SLA.
[05:12] Jenna: noted. we'll surface standard DPA and SLA templates.
[05:20] Ethan: one technical question — how does your KV cache/prefix caching work with a multi-tenant setup? we want to avoid cross-tenant contamination and understand eviction semantics.
[05:33] Ravi: good point. our runtime isolates KV caches by deployment and tenant id; eviction is LRU with configurable memory caps. in Dedicated we can pin model shards and tune cache sizes for high reuse workloads. small transcription glitch: we sometimes say KV cash in the call notes.
[05:55] Sophie: curious about encryption in transit — do you support mutual TLS or just standard TLS?
[06:03] Tara: we support mTLS for Private and Dedicated peered deployments; hosted API supports TLS and you can optionally set client certs for extra validation.
[06:16] Maria: for data residency, can we keep inference in our VPC for EU traffic only?
[06:23] Ravi: yes — you can route by region and policy. for Private deployments we can isolate regions, and for Hosted we can ensure EU-only model endpoints in eu-west-1. we'll document routing policies.
[06:40] [00:07:00] Jenna: i'm going to walk through a very brief onboarding checklist: 1) access & SSO: who needs seats and SSO mapping; 2) networking: VPC peering and firewall allowlist; 3) compliance: docs requested; 4) pilot metrics: what to measure; 5) runbook and escalation paths.
[07:05] Maria: SSO will be SAML via Okta, we have 10 initial users — engineering and security.
[07:12] Jenna: okta is supported, we'll share the SSO mapping doc.
[07:20] Ethan: for the pilot env, what's the typical time to provision Dedicated GPU pool?
[07:26] Ravi: with reserved capacity templates it's usually 3-5 business days for a small Dedicated pool, less if you're ok with a burst-backed trial. We can also do an isolated Private dev cluster but that takes longer — 2-3 weeks.
[07:45] Maria: given our timeline I'd prefer Dedicated for the pilot and evaluate Private later.
[07:52] Jenna: sounds reasonable. a couple of common objections: cost vs latency — if you opt for quantized models to save cost you'll sometimes see slight quality delta; we'll need your eval prompts to measure.
[08:05] Maria: yes we'll share prompts.
[08:09] Ethan: any limitations on SDK integrations? we currently call model endpoint via gRPC and REST; need low-latency streaming.
[08:18] Ravi: we support REST and streaming websockets for chat and have a gRPC beta — we can enable webhook-style streaming if you need. we'll check lower-level TLS tuning with your infra.
[08:31] [00:10:00] Tara: ops-wise, who will be the day-to-day contacts? Jenna: i'll handle commercial; tara will manage onboarding; ravi for technical. maria?
[08:44] Maria: i'll be the project lead. Ethan will be day-to-day infra contact, Sophie will own security questions, Liam exec sponsor.
[08:53] Jenna: perfect. action items recap: ravi will send the network checklist; jenny — note, jenna will send pricing and SOW; tara sends the onboarding runbook.
[09:10] Liam: quick risk question: how do you handle PII deletion requests — can you purge logs and training traces?
[09:19] Tara: yes we have data retention controls and deletion APIs; for Private we can guarantee zero retention if desired; for hosted we can configure retention windows and purge requests. we'll include specifics in the DPA.
[09:32] Sophie: will you support a pen-test or security questionnaire? we'll need an SSP and answers for our vendor risk.
[09:39] Jenna: yes — we can provide an SSP, SOC2 attestation, and answer an initial security questionnaire; we sometimes run a joint pen-test for Private deployments.
[09:51] [00:15:00] Maria: okay let's talk about the pilot acceptance criteria again, and how we'll measure A/B tests. for the classifier we have labeled datasets; we want to run an offline evaluation and then an online canary for 24 hours.
[10:12] Ravi: sounds good — we can help with offline eval harness (we have a simple script) and provide canary routing templates so you can route small % of traffic.
[10:22] Ethan: regarding storage for embeddings, do you prefer pushing vectors to your managed vector DB or do customers keep them in-house?
[10:31] Tara: both — we integrate with managed vector stores and also provide an embeddings-only API so you can store vectors in your own store. for PII concerns many financial customers store vectors in their own VPC.
[10:48] Maria: important: if vectors are stored externally we need deterministic hashing and redaction policies.
[10:56] Ravi: understood — we'll include our hashing and redaction recommendations.
[11:03] [00:20:00] Jenna: timeline again — pilot starts week of 2026-06-07, 2 weeks, then readout week of 2026-06-21. procurement and security review to run in parallel. does that align?
[11:17] Liam: yes that aligns, procurement will need the pricing sheet and SOW by end of next week.
[11:25] Jenna: we'll get that out.
[11:30] Maria: one more question — observability. does your console expose token-level traces for specific user requests? we want to debug hallucinations and token generation path.
[11:40] Ravi: we provide token-level latency and cost traces and request/response logs with redaction for PII; patch-level tracing is available in Private via tracing headers.
[11:52] Sophie: for forensic purposes, can logs be exported to our SIEM in real time?
[11:58] Tara: yes, via our log streaming connector to Splunk or S3 forwarders.
[12:05] [00:25:00] Ethan: slight tangent — compatibility matrix for model variants, quantization and GPUs (A100 vs H100)? we saw mixed perf numbers.
[12:15] Ravi: we have a model catalog with verified profiles per hardware. H100 gives the best throughput and perf for large context, A100 is still performant for many chat workloads. we recommend H100 for heavy batch inference but for cost-sensitive you can use quantized on A100 or T4 for embeddings. we'll share the profile sheet.
[12:33] Maria: thank you.
[12:36] Jenna: okay, i want to call out a couple of risks we usually surface: 1) under-specified success metrics; 2) networking delays during peering; 3) latent security questionnaire turnaround. mitigate by agreeing on an evaluation plan and having security Qs upfront.
[12:58] Maria: agreed, we'll prioritize the security questionnaire.
[13:05] [00:35:00] Ravi: operationally, during the pilot we can set autoscaling guardrails and observability alerts so you don't hit a surprise. we can also run a synthetic load test to validate p95 latency under your expected qps.
[13:20] Ethan: synthetic test would be helpful. schedule it during low-production hours, we can provide test tenants.
[13:28] Jenna: note, we'll need test tokens and masking for PII.
[13:34] Sophie: also, for compliance, we want a read-only audit path for logs — no one should be able to modify audit records.
[13:42] Tara: we have immutable audit exports when configured to S3 with object lock; we can walk through that.
[13:50] [00:45:00] Maria: next steps recap from our side: we will share prompts and labeled datasets, security questionnaire, and Okta SSO contact.
[13:59] Liam: procurement will want the SOW and pricing, include options for Dedicated reserve and 12-month committed discounts.
[14:08] Jenna: will do. ravi will send network checklist and the model perf sheet, tara will send onboarding runbook, and i will send SOW and security docs.
[14:20] Ethan: can we get a scheduled follow-up demo/hand-on with the SE to validate the flows?
[14:26] Ravi: yes we'll schedule a technical deep dive next week — i'll email 3 slots.
[14:33] Sophie: one last note, competitor question — we've been looking at SageAI and StratusEndpoints for dedicated inference. what do customers cite as main differentiator?
[14:44] Jenna: customers often call out our unified runtime across Hosted/Dedicated/Private and the tooling for cost/perf tradeoffs — intelligent batching, fallback routing, and the console visibility. also enterprise SLAs for Dedicated.
[14:58] Maria: good to know.
[15:02] [00:55:00] Tara: final quick Q: who should we put on the invite for the technical deep dive? ethan and maria plus maybe one infra engineer and one data scientist. ravi: noted.
[15:12] Jenna: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in writing with the artifacts. any objections to the proposed pilot start week of 2026-06-07?
[15:20] Maria: none from us.
[15:24] Jenna: great, thanks all — talk soon.

Meeting end.

Attached references mentioned: network checklist (link will be shared), SOC2 + SSP, model perf profiles (H100/A100), onboarding runbook, SOW template.

Transcript notes: occasional misattribution and transcription errors (e.g., KV cash -> KV cache, redwood-infer -> Redwood Dedicated).
